reasons: Lake identity verifies United States v. Jacobsen, U.S. Supreme Court, decided 1984-04-02, year 1984.
Lake citations match the asserted official citation 466 U.S. 109, neutral cite 1984 U.S. LEXIS 53, and parallel cites 104 S. Ct. 1652; 80 L. Ed. 2d 85; 52 U.S.L.W. 4414.
The opinion defines a property seizure as meaningful interference with possessory interests.
The opinion says the Fourth Amendment proscribes only governmental action and is inapplicable to private searches not involving the government.

The opinion supports the private-search proposition by testing government conduct by the degree to which it exceeded the private search and by holding that the agent's visual inspection learned nothing not already learned during the private search.
residual_risks: The proposition should remain tied to the already-frustrated privacy interest and should not be read to validate government conduct exceeding the private search.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Say: government inspection within the scope of the prior private search invades no remaining legitimate privacy interest to the extent that interest has already been frustrated.

defect.proposed_fix: Keep the case on the page only with a qualifier that it anchors the private-search doctrine component, not foreign-search doctrine.
